445	def _required_when_field_errors(record, field_errors, required_when):
446	    """Check every declared ``required_when`` condition over final values.
447	
448	    Runs after structure checks, marker matching, default filling, type
449	    conversion and the enum, range, pattern and lte_field checks. A
450	    condition is skipped when either participating field already carries
451	    an error; the original errors are kept and every other condition on
452	    the row is still checked. Conditions are evaluated in schema column
453	    order and returned as ``(name, message)`` pairs so the caller can
454	    file each error under its declaring column's position. The rule
455	    fires only when the condition column's final boolean is true and the
456	    declaring column's final value is null -- a false or null condition
457	    never fires, and a final 0 or false on the declaring column counts
458	    as a value. A violation names ``required_when``, both output names
459	    and the true condition value.
460	    """
461	    errors = []
462	    for name, target in required_when:
463	        if name in field_errors or target in field_errors:
464	            continue
465	        if record.get(target) is not True:
466	            continue
467	        if record.get(name) is not None:
468	            continue
469	        errors.append((
470	            name,
471	            f"{name}: value is null but required_when {target!r} is true"))
472	    return errors

475	def _prepare_lte_fields(columns):

561	def _prepare_patterns(columns, defaults, value_maps=frozenset()):
562	    """Validate the optional ``pattern`` regular expression of each column.
563	
564	    Returns a mapping of output field name to the compiled expression; the
565	    declared expression text is kept verbatim (``compiled.pattern`` hands
566	    it back) and the match later covers the whole string under Python's
567	    standard ``re`` semantics -- case-sensitive by default, with inline
568	    flags such as ``(?i)`` honored. The attribute must be a non-blank
569	    string and may appear only on a ``string`` column; a non-string or
570	    whitespace-only value, a declaration on an ``integer`` or ``boolean``
571	    column, or an expression the ``re`` compiler rejects is a
572	    configuration error. A processed ``default`` (already trimmed and, for
573	    an NFKC column, normalized) that does not match is a configuration
574	    error even when no row needs it, while an ``allowed_values`` entry
575	    that fails the expression is not. When the column declares a
576	    ``value_map`` the filled default is itself mapped once, so the
577	    constraint is checked against the mapped target. Raises ValueError
578	    naming ``pattern``, the output field and the offending value (the
579	    default error also names ``default``) before the input is read; the
580	    caller's schema is never mutated.
581	    """
582	    patterns = {}
583	    for column in columns:
584	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
585	        if "pattern" not in column:
586	            continue
587	        pattern = column["pattern"]
588	        if not isinstance(pattern, str):
589	            raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} must be a string")
590	        if not pattern.strip():
591	            raise ValueError(
592	                f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} must be a non-blank string")
593	        if kind != "string":
594	            raise ValueError(
595	                f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} requires a string column")
596	        try:
597	            compiled = re.compile(pattern)
598	        except re.error as exc:
599	            raise ValueError(
600	                f"column {name!r} pattern {pattern!r} is not a valid regular "
601	                f"expression: {exc}") from None
602	        patterns[name] = compiled
603	        if name in defaults:
604	            effective_default = defaults[name]
605	            column_map = value_maps.get(name)
606	            if column_map is not None:
607	                effective_default = _mapped_string(effective_default, column_map)
608	            if compiled.fullmatch(effective_default) is None:
609	                raise ValueError(
610	                    f"column {name!r} default {effective_default!r} does not match "
611	                    f"pattern {pattern!r}")
612	    return patterns

652	def _prepare_boolean_aliases(columns):
653	    """Validate the optional ``boolean_aliases`` mapping of each boolean column.
654	
655	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh dict keyed by the
656	    normalized alias text (the declared key trimmed and Unicode
657	    casefolded) holding the target boolean verbatim. The attribute must be
658	    a non-empty object and may appear only on a ``boolean`` column; every
659	    key must be a non-blank string and every mapped value a boolean. Two
660	    keys that normalize to the same text are invalid even when they map to
661	    the same boolean, and a key normalizing to ``true`` or ``false`` is
662	    refused so the built-in spellings keep their fixed meaning. Raises
663	    ValueError naming ``boolean_aliases``, the output field and the
664	    offending value before the input is read; the caller's schema is never
665	    mutated.
666	    """
667	    aliases = {}
668	    for column in columns:
669	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
670	        if "boolean_aliases" not in column:
671	            continue
672	        configured = column["boolean_aliases"]
673	        if kind != "boolean":
674	            raise ValueError(
675	                f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases {configured!r} requires a boolean column")
676	        if not isinstance(configured, dict) or not configured:
677	            raise ValueError(
678	                f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases {configured!r} must be a non-empty object")
679	        normalized = {}
680	        for key, mapped in configured.items():
681	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
682	                raise ValueError(
683	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} must be a non-blank string")
684	            if not isinstance(mapped, bool):
685	                raise ValueError(
686	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases value {mapped!r} for key {key!r} "
687	                    "must be a boolean")
688	            folded = key.strip().casefold()
689	            if folded in ("true", "false"):
690	                raise ValueError(
691	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} must not normalize to "
692	                    f"the built-in boolean spelling {folded!r}")
693	            if folded in normalized:
694	                raise ValueError(
695	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} normalizes to a repeated "
696	                    f"key {folded!r}")
697	            normalized[folded] = mapped
698	        aliases[name] = normalized
699	    return aliases

702	def _validate_schema_structure(schema):
703	    """Validate the structural shape of the schema before any file is read.
704	
705	    The schema must be an object holding a non-empty ``columns`` list;
706	    each column must be an object carrying ``name`` (a non-blank string,
707	    kept verbatim -- never trimmed -- and unique case-sensitively) and
708	    ``type`` (one of ``string``, ``integer``, ``boolean``), plus an
709	    optional ``required`` that, when present, must be a boolean. Checks
710	    run top level first, then column by column in order (column
711	    structure, name, duplicate name, type, required) and only the first
712	    problem is reported: the ValueError message names ``schema`` and the
713	    one-based column position, names a missing key, carries the
714	    offending value verbatim, and points a duplicate name at the later
715	    column. Unknown attributes are ignored and the caller's schema is
716	    never mutated.
717	    """
718	    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
719	        raise ValueError(f"schema must be an object, got {schema!r}")
720	    if "columns" not in schema:
721	        raise ValueError("schema is missing 'columns'")
722	    columns = schema["columns"]
723	    if not isinstance(columns, list) or not columns:
724	        raise ValueError(f"schema 'columns' must be a non-empty list, got {columns!r}")
725	    seen = {}
726	    for index, column in enumerate(columns, start=1):
727	        if not isinstance(column, dict):
728	            raise ValueError(f"schema column {index} must be an object, got {column!r}")
729	        for key in ("name", "type"):
730	            if key not in column:
731	                raise ValueError(f"schema column {index} is missing {key!r}")
732	        name = column["name"]
733	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
734	            raise ValueError(
735	                f"schema column {index} name {name!r} must be a non-blank string")
736	        if name in seen:
737	            raise ValueError(
738	                f"schema column {index} name {name!r} duplicates column {seen[name]}")
739	        seen[name] = index
740	        kind = column["type"]
741	        if kind not in ("string", "integer", "boolean"):
742	            raise ValueError(
743	                f"schema column {index} type {kind!r} must be one of "
744	                "'string', 'integer', 'boolean'")
745	        if "required" in column and not isinstance(column["required"], bool):
746	            raise ValueError(
747	                f"schema column {index} required {column['required']!r} must be a boolean")
748

750	def _prepare_schema(schema):
751	    _validate_schema_structure(schema)
752	    columns = schema["columns"]
753	    normalizing = _prepare_unicode_normalization(columns)
754	    casefolding = _prepare_casefold(columns)
755	    collapsing = _prepare_collapse_whitespace(columns)
756	    value_maps = _prepare_value_maps(columns, normalizing, collapsing, casefolding)
757	    defaults = _prepare_defaults(columns, normalizing, collapsing, casefolding)
758	    allowed = _prepare_allowed_values(columns, defaults, value_maps)
759	    markers = _prepare_missing_values(columns)
760	    aliases = _prepare_boolean_aliases(columns)
761	    ranges = _prepare_ranges(columns, defaults)
762	    lte_fields = _prepare_lte_fields(columns)
763	    patterns = _prepare_patterns(columns, defaults, value_maps)
764	    sources = []
765	    for column in columns:
766	        name = column["name"]
767	        if "source" not in column:
768	            sources.append(name)
769	            continue
770	        origin = column["source"]
771	        if not isinstance(origin, str) or not origin.strip():
772	            raise ValueError(f"column {name!r}: source must be a non-empty, non-blank string")
773	        sources.append(origin)
774	    owners = {}
775	    for column, origin in zip(columns, sources):
776	        name = column["name"]
777	        if origin in owners:
778	            raise ValueError(f"columns {owners[origin]!r} and {name!r} share source {origin!r}")
779	        owners[origin] = name
780	    # The required_when references are validated only after every
781	    # pre-existing configuration check (structure, per-column attributes
782	    # and sources) has passed.
783	    required_when = _prepare_required_when(columns)
784	    return columns, sources, defaults, allowed, markers, aliases, ranges, lte_fields, normalizing, patterns, casefolding, required_when, value_maps, collapsing

845	    """Group accepted records by the converted values of duplicate_by fields."""
846	    groups = {}

857	def _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns):
858	    """Validate the optional single-field equality filter.
859	
860	    The condition is an object with exactly ``field`` and ``value`` keys;
861	    field matches an output name literally (source aliases are not
862	    recognized) and value must fit the target type, with null allowed for
863	    every type. Returns (field, value) or None when filtering is disabled.
864	    Raises ValueError before the input is read.
865	    """
866	    if filter_eq is None:
867	        return None

869	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must be an object with 'field' and 'value' keys")
870	    keys = set(filter_eq)
871	    if keys != {"field", "value"}:
872	        details = []
873	        missing = [key for key in ("field", "value") if key not in keys]
874	        extra = sorted(keys - {"field", "value"})
875	        if missing:
876	            details.append("missing key(s): " + ", ".join(missing))
877	        if extra:
878	            details.append("unexpected key(s): " + ", ".join(extra))
879	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must contain exactly 'field' and 'value' keys (" + "; ".join(details) + ")")
880	    field = filter_eq["field"]
881	    if not isinstance(field, str):
882	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a string")
883	    if not field.strip():
884	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a non-blank string")
885	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
886	    if field not in by_name:
887	        raise ValueError(f"filter_eq field {field!r} is not a schema column name")
888	    value = filter_eq["value"]

965	def _prepare_filter_range(filter_range, columns):
966	    """Validate the optional single-field inclusive integer range filter.
967	
968	    The condition is an object holding ``field`` plus at least one of
969	    ``minimum`` and ``maximum`` and no other keys; field matches an output
970	    name literally (source aliases are not recognized) and must name an
971	    ``integer`` column. Each declared bound must be a non-boolean integer
972	    (negative values and zero are legal) and is used verbatim -- never
973	    converted; a missing end imposes no limit on that side, equal ends
974	    accept exactly that one integer, and a minimum greater than the
975	    maximum is a configuration error. Returns (field, minimum, maximum)
976	    with None for an undeclared end, or None when filtering is disabled.

978	    before the input is read; the caller's condition is never mutated.

980	    if filter_range is None:
981	        return None
982	    if not isinstance(filter_range, dict):
983	        raise ValueError(
984	            f"filter_range {filter_range!r} must be an object with 'field' and "
985	            "'minimum' and/or 'maximum' keys")
986	    keys = set(filter_range)
987	    allowed = ("field", "minimum", "maximum")
988	    if "field" not in keys or not keys & {"minimum", "maximum"} or keys - set(allowed):
989	        details = []
990	        missing = []
991	        if "field" not in keys:
992	            missing.append("field")
993	        if not keys & {"minimum", "maximum"}:
994	            missing.append("minimum or maximum")
995	        extra = sorted(keys - set(allowed))
996	        if missing:
